items_missed: Set the Agenda: never asked "how are you today," and while she described what she'd cover (info, then pricing, then an estimate) she never gave a rough time estimate or got an explicit "sound good?" confirmation before diving in.

Probe: never asked about special considerations (narrow hallways, tight turns), packing needs, box count, or moving stressors; also never got destination-address stairs/floors or proactively asked about parking/HOA access -- the customer volunteered the "not gated, on the street" detail unprompted.

Quote/Booking: the call ended in a transfer before any quote or booking happened -- no deposit mention, no bolded confirmation-email recap, no "reply with corrections," no final "any other questions before I let you go," and no branch hours or contact info given.
Politeness: used the customer's name ("Stephanie") only once across the whole call, well short of the 3+ threshold.

Bonus: kept collecting full address details for a third stop after already learning the home was 1,800 sq ft -- over her stated 1,600 sq ft cutoff -- instead of recognizing the transfer was needed and handing off sooner; beyond one light aside about the customer's email address ("That's cute"), there was no real rapport-building.
top_strength: Bri kept the intake organized and low-friction under a messy multi-stop move -- she calmly untangled a three-location job (home, a personal storage/warehouse swap, and a third address) and proactively told the customer "no need to take notes, I can send you an email after we talk through everything," which took pressure off the customer right away.
coaching_note: You caught the 1,800 sq ft home in the first probing question but kept gathering a whole third address before transferring -- once you know a move is over your 1,600 sq ft cutoff, hand it off right away so you're not spending the customer's time on details someone else will have to re-collect. You also only said Stephanie's name once the entire call; use it a few more times to build warmth, especially since this is a repeat customer who's proud of coming back a third time -- that was a moment to lean into rapport, not just note the discount question and move on. Last thing: give a real agenda statement up front ("this'll take about 10 minutes, sound good?") so the customer knows what to expect before you start asking for details.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and cooperative throughout with one genuine light moment ("That's cute" about the email address), but mostly transactional address-and-detail collection with inconsistent warmth and only a single use of the customer's name.
